question: Can geometric Brownian motion provide a coherent multiplicative diffusion model for positive data, a tractable score-matching loss, and image samples competitive enough to justify the claimed link to Dale-compatible learning?

key_findings.claim: The paper derives two reverse-time samplers from element-wise geometric Brownian motion: an ambient-space sign-agnostic update and a log-space sign-preserving Dale-Langevin update.
key_findings.evidence: The GBM transition is conditionally log-normal. Applying the reverse-SDE formula gives a state-scaled score term; a Lamperti log transform followed by Euler-Maruyama yields an exponential update that cannot change a coordinate's sign.

key_findings.claim: Multiplicative denoising score matching is the paper's strongest self-contained technical contribution.
key_findings.evidence: The model learns the state-weighted score x times grad log p. Theorem 4.1 and Appendix B show that its conditional denoising objective differs from the marginal explicit objective only by a parameter-independent constant under regularity and boundary assumptions; non-negative score matching appears at time zero.

key_findings.claim: The EGD connection is structural rather than evidence that the image generator is biologically plausible.
key_findings.evidence: The same negative-entropy mirror map produces multiplicative, sign-preserving exponentiated updates in EGD and mirrored Langevin dynamics, but EGD acts on synaptic weights while the proposed sampler acts on image-state coordinates; the paper explicitly notes that distinction.

anchors.section: 5.1 Exponentiated Gradient Descent and Dale's Law

key_findings.claim: The experiments establish generative capability, not competitiveness with modern diffusion models.
key_findings.evidence: The study reports only the two proposed samplers and two initialization modes on MNIST-family data and CIFAR-10. There is no matched DDPM, score-SDE, beta-diffusion, or gamma-diffusion baseline. CIFAR-10 FID improves from roughly 86-101 without terminal denoising to 38.6-51.6 after 16-25 extra denoising steps, so a crucial quality gain is post-processing dependent.

key_findings.claim: The terminal prior and annealing design leave a material unconditional-generation ambiguity.
key_findings.evidence: One initialization passes class-average images through the finite forward process and therefore carries class-structured information; the alternative fits a log-normal approximation to forward terminal samples rather than demonstrating convergence to a data-independent prior. The visual ablation shows chi=0.995 produces clean but collapsed CIFAR samples, chi=1.0 produces diverse but heavily noisy samples, and chi=0.9995 trades between them.

key_findings.claim: The appendix identifies discretization bias but does not correct or quantify it in the reported image results.
key_findings.evidence: For a log-normal target, the Euler-Maruyama mirrored-Langevin chain converges to the right log-mean but an inflated log-covariance depending on the step size. The experiments tune step size and repeated inner steps by FID/KID rather than testing bias calibration.

anchors.section: D Mirrored Langevin Dynamics for a Log-normal Target
D limiting measure and E.1 Training Details

method.core_idea: Replace additive Gaussian corruption with proportional geometric-Brownian corruption so positivity, log-normal marginals, multiplicative scores, and sign-preserving reverse updates arise from one SDE.
method.mechanism: Sample conditionally log-normal forward states, train a neural network with the multiplicative denoising score loss, and integrate either the ambient reverse SDE or its Lamperti-transformed log-space SDE using empirically annealed noise and optional terminal denoising.
assumptions: The modeled data can be shifted or scaled into a strictly positive orthant without harming its geometry.
The finite forward horizon produces a terminal distribution that can be approximated by the chosen fitted log-normal initializer.
The density and score satisfy the regularity, finite-moment, and boundary conditions used in the score-matching equivalence.
Euler-Maruyama and annealing error are small enough that the continuous reverse-SDE argument remains predictive.
FID and KID on low-resolution image benchmarks measure the intended benefit of multiplicative dynamics.

techniques.role: Makes perturbations proportional to state magnitude and keeps positive data positive.
Turns GBM into an additive log-space process and exposes the sign-preserving sampler.
Learns the state-multiplied score needed by the multiplicative reverse dynamics.
Connects the negative-entropy mirror map behind EGD to Dale-Langevin dynamics.
Reduces injected noise across reverse levels, trading sample diversity against fidelity.

evaluations.setting: MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and Kuzushiji-MNIST with NCSN-Deeper.
evaluations.metric: FID, KID, uncurated samples, and nearest-neighbor inspection.
evaluations.result: Both samplers generate recognizable images; class-average initialization generally improves FID, while Fashion-MNIST shows underrepresented modes.
evaluations.baseline: The two proposed samplers and two initialization choices; no external generative baseline.

evaluations.setting: CIFAR-10 with DDPM++ and exponential-moving-average checkpoints.
evaluations.metric: FID and KID over generated and test samples.
evaluations.result: Best reported FID is 38.562 for Dale-Langevin with class-average initialization and 25 terminal steps; without those steps its FID is 88.322.
evaluations.baseline: Sign-agnostic versus Dale-Langevin, class-average versus fitted log-normal initialization.

evaluations.metric: Qualitative fidelity, diversity, residual noise, and mode coverage.
evaluations.result: Chi=0.995 is clean but collapsed, chi=1.0 is diverse but noisy, and chi=0.9995 is a middle ground.
evaluations.baseline: Three annealing factors with the sampler step size and inner-loop count fixed.

limitations: No external diffusion or generative-model baseline supports a state-of-the-art or efficiency claim.
Class-average initialization is data- and class-dependent, so it is weaker evidence for unconditional sampling from a simple prior.
The fitted log-normal terminal prior is empirical; finite-time convergence or terminal mismatch is not measured.
CIFAR quality depends strongly on extra terminal denoising steps chosen per sampler.
Hyperparameters are selected on 1,024 generated samples by the same FID/KID family used for reporting, with no held-out selection protocol described.
The claimed neuroscience motivation concerns weight updates, whereas experiments diffuse pixels and do not test a biological prediction.
The paper notes discretization bias but provides no bias-corrected sampler or calibration study.
failure_modes: Zero-valued or signed data violate the strict-positive log transform unless an arbitrary preprocessing offset is introduced.
The forward horizon retains too much source structure, so apparent sample quality comes from initialization leakage.
Aggressive annealing suppresses noise and collapses modes; weak annealing leaves high-frequency noise.
State-weighted scores become poorly conditioned near zero or on heavy-tailed coordinates.
Euler discretization accumulates the log-covariance bias derived in Appendix D.
Perceptual quality degrades sharply when moving beyond small, low-resolution datasets.
reusable_insights: Choose a forward process whose state constraints and terminal law match the domain instead of defaulting to additive Gaussian noise.
Audit a diffusion model's terminal prior separately from its reverse solver; a tractable conditional transition does not prove a data-independent endpoint.
When a sampler needs terminal cleanup, report pre-cleanup and post-cleanup cost-quality curves and treat cleanup as part of the method.
A shared mirror map can unify an optimizer and a sampler mathematically without making their application-level semantics equivalent.
Visual diversity-fidelity phase diagrams can reveal annealing failures that a single best FID hides.
open_questions: Can a likelihood, ELBO, or probability-flow formulation quantify terminal-prior and discretization error for GBM diffusion?
How does the method compare with Gaussian, gamma, beta, and conservative multiplicative diffusion under identical networks and compute?
Can the sampler handle genuine zeros and mixed signs without offset-dependent results?
Does a higher-order or Metropolis-corrected integrator remove the log-covariance bias at practical cost?
Which real multiplicative-noise domains benefit after controlling for the log transform alone?
Does the EGD connection yield any testable biological prediction beyond sign preservation?

competitive_landscape.title: Multiplicative Diffusion Models: Beyond Gaussian Latents
competitive_landscape.difference: Gruhlke et al. use skew-symmetric multiplicative noise that preserves the data-norm distribution, prove exponential convergence to a non-Gaussian latent, and target heavy tails; Dale-Langevin uses GBM, positivity, log-normal marginals, and image generation.

competitive_landscape.title: Tweedie's Formulae and Diffusion Generative Models Beyond Gaussian
competitive_landscape.difference: Tang et al. derive non-Gaussian Tweedie identities and denoising objectives for GBM, squared-Bessel, and CIR processes and evaluate images and finance, broadening and independently testing the GBM score-matching direction.

competitive_landscape.title: A diffusion-based generative model for financial time series via geometric Brownian motion
competitive_landscape.difference: Kim et al. also use GBM and denoising score matching but focus on heteroskedastic financial sequences with a Transformer and stylized-fact evaluation rather than a Dale/EGD interpretation or image sampling.

competitive_landscape.title: Beta Diffusion
competitive_landscape.difference: Beta Diffusion uses multiplicative beta transitions and KL upper bounds for range-bounded data; the reviewed paper uses GBM and score matching for strictly positive unbounded data.

competitive_landscape.title: Denoising Diffusion Gamma Models
competitive_landscape.difference: DDGM replaces Gaussian perturbations with gamma noise and reports image and speech generation; it lacks the reverse-SDE/mirror-map construction but supplies an essential non-Gaussian empirical baseline.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: This is a complete GBM-based multiplicative generative framework and the first biologically inspired multiplicative generator founded on Dale-compatible exponentiated updates.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper derives forward and reverse SDEs, two samplers, an equivalent denoising score loss, the mirror-descent connection, and low-resolution image experiments.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The GBM score objective and explicit EGD/mirrored-Langevin synthesis are coherent and useful. The biological framing is mainly an analogy, and missing matched baselines, terminal-prior tests, and discretization controls prevent the experiments from establishing superiority over other constrained or non-Gaussian diffusion families.

reviewer_notes: Read all 47 extracted pages, including the complete proof, bias derivation, hyperparameter tables, nearest-neighbor sheets, and every annealing/sample figure. Visually inspected the main score table and CIFAR annealing grid. Primary arXiv and OpenReview competitor records were checked on 2026-08-23.
